newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban church seeks live TV broadcast of papal mass.
newsitem.headline: Cuban church seeks live TV broadcast of papal mass.

text.p: Cuba's Roman Catholic church said on Thursday it has asked the government to allow live transmission on state television of one of the papal masses during Pope John Paul II's visit to the island next January.

Father Jose Felix Perez, secretary of the church's commission organising the visit and also a member of the joint church-state commission formed to plan the trip, said the request for a live media transmission had been made to the government and was being studied by authorities.

Perez was speaking at a news conference after Cuba's Cardinal Jaime Ortega formally opened with a blessing a house that the church commission will use as its planning centre. The Cuban state has lent the house, in a residential district of Havana, to the church for the purpose.

Live transmission of a mass would be an extraordinary event in a communist-ruled country where all media is state controlled and where speeches broadcast are generally those of President Fidel Castro and other senior political figures.

Perez said that ahead of the visit the church would also like to see Cardinal Ortega and other Cuban bishops allowed to appear on state television to to inform the Cuban people about the Jan. 21-25 visit and its significance.

The papal visit was agreed at a historic first meeting between the pontiff and President Fidel Castro in November last year at the Vatican. That encounter marked a clear improvement in ties between the Catholic Church and the Cuban authorities over the past year.
In a sign of these improved relations, authorities have allowed the church to celebrate a mass in the open air in Havana this Sunday.

The mass, to to be celebrated in the square outside Havana cathedral from an altar erected at the entrance to the building, will be the first religious service to be held outside a church in Cuba in more than 35 years, chuch officials said.
Perez, who called the permission a "very encouraging sign", said the request for the outdoor mass had been made as Havana cathedral was being restored ahead of the papal visit.

The pontiff is set to make trips to the central and eastern provincial cities of Santa Clara, Camaguey and Santiago de Cuba during his stay in Cuba, the only Spanish-speaking country in Latin America that he has not yet visited.
